Alright, let me think this through.

---

I'm 49, been farming since my twenties. Finished primary school, that's it. My wife and I do most of the work on the 90 mu. Our older boy works in Handan now — sends money home, but he comes back for wheat harvest if he can. Daughter-in-law helps when she's not looking after the grandchildren.

I split the land like this: about 60 mu for wheat-maize like most folks around here, and 30 mu for stevia because the Yang family across the lane has been making real money on it for years. I watched them three, four seasons before I tried it myself — that was maybe eight years back. The sugar factory pays decent if the leaves are dry and clean.

**Wheat** — I plant around October 5th to 10th, after the maize comes off. Jimai 22 mostly, sometimes save seed from last year if it looked good, otherwise buy from the supply shop. Before planting I spread about 40 kg of 15-15-15 compound per mu — that's two bags for every three mu, roughly. Then at jointing in March I put down urea, about 15 kg a mu. If the wheat's pale I give it a bit more, you can see it in the field. Water maybe three times — once before winter if it's dry, once at jointing, once at filling. My well runs fine but the electricity adds up, maybe 20 yuan each watering per mu. Last year I got around 450 kg a mu, that was a decent year.

**Maize** — Right after wheat harvest, middle of June, you have to hustle. I hire the combine for wheat, then the rotary tiller comes through, then I plant within a week. Zhengdan 958 or whatever hybrid the shop has — about 3 kg a mu, costs roughly 50 yuan. Put starter compound with the seeder, then topdress urea at knee-high, about 20 kg a mu. If July and August rain enough I don't water; if it's dry I'll give it one or two. Last year around 500 kg a mu.

**Stevia** — Different work altogether. I transplant seedlings end of April. Needs more feeding than the grains — I put 50 kg of compound in the base, then urea twice during the growing. Weeding is the killer, you can't use the same herbicides as on wheat, so I hire help from the village — maybe 10 people-days per mu across the season. Two cuts, sometimes three, dry the leaves in the sun, sell to the factory. Costs a lot more upfront but if the price holds it pays better than maize.

I'm doing mostly the same as last year. When things work you don't go changing them — my neighbor tried switching his stevia to peanuts two years ago and lost money. I'll keep watching what others do but I'm not jumping.
